q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a _____.
e: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a circle, such as artificial satellites going around the earth.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an _____.
e: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis, like the rotation of earth about its own axis.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not _____ or change shape.
e: A rigid body is defined as a body that does not deform or change shape regardless of how it moves.

q: In a rigid body, the distance between any two particles within the body remains _____.
e: For a rigid body, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant no matter how the body moves.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo _____ motion about a common axis.
e: All particles constituting a rigid body in rotational motion undergo circular motion about a common axis.

q: When an object rotates and its angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the motion is called the rotational motion under constant angular _____.
e: If angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant, defining rotational motion under constant angular acceleration.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=$ _____.
e: The initial angular speed is defined as the magnitude of the angular velocity of the object at time $t=0$.

q: The equations for constant angular acceleration in rotational motion are _____ to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion.
e: The kinematic equations for constant angular acceleration are analogous to those for constant linear acceleration.

q: Average angular speed is expressed as $\omega = \frac{\omega + \omega_0}{_____}$.
e: The formula for average angular speed under constant acceleration is the sum of initial and final angular speeds divided by 2.

q: The rotation of earth about its own axis creates the cycle of _____.
e: The rotation of the earth about its own axis is an example of rotational motion that creates the cycle of day and night.

q: If its angular velocity changes at a constant rate, then we can say that the angular acceleration is _____.
e: A constant rate of change in angular velocity means the angular acceleration is constant.

q: In Grade 11, the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of an object in _____ motion have been learnt.
e: The textbook notes that angular variables for an object in circular motion were previously learnt in Grade 11.
